One note on it: I DONT WANT ANY DEPRECATION/BACKWARDS-COMPAT ANYWHERE -- deprecated code is to be REMOVED [...] Assistant: The corrected position now matches the repo's doctrine, and your note makes the rule even harder than the agent's amendment (it still says "marked `#[deprecated]`" as if that's a tolerable waypoint — it isn't). Let me verify the current code state, capture your rule in memory, and make sure the deletion is tracked as an issue rather than narrated.

Assistant: Done. The agent's corrected position is right, and your no-deprecation rule is now captured and actioned:

**Filed [#2770](https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/issues/2770)** — delete `NmpApp::open_observed_feed_source` outright. I verified the current state first: the method is public, marked `#[deprecated]`, and its doc comment still calls it "the correct doorway" for raw `ObservedProjectionSink` hooks — exactly the blessed-escape-hatch state you're forbidding. #2723 shipped only the deprecation signal and closed; nobody ever filed the deletion. Its only in-repo callers are its own tests, so the Rust-side delete is cheap; the real work item is the podcast-player `ObservedProjectionSink` dependency, which the issue routes to a named concept-owned read (sibling of #2758) instead of a retained doorway. The issue also includes the ratchet: a doctrine-lint gate banning `#[deprecated]` from all non-generated workspace code, so "deprecated-but-blessed" becomes unrepresentable rather than a thing agents re-invent. (The only other `#[deprecated]` markers in the tree are flatc-generated FlatBuffers boilerplate, which the gate exempts.)

**Memory updated** — `feedback_no_compat_aliases` now states the stronger form: no deprecation/backwards-compat anywhere, `#[deprecated]` is itself a violation to delete on sight, not a transitional state. [...] - New doctrine-lint rule `feed_vocabulary` (`crates/nmp-testing/bin/doctrine-lint/rules/feed_vocabulary.rs`) — a targeted token-ban ratchet (matches the existing `deleted_defaults`/`nip29_kind_blind` idiom) scoped to `nmp-native-runtime`, `nmp-uniffi-support`, `nmp-browser-runtime`, and the `nmp-codegen` feed-helper templates, with real positive/negative fixtures and a scope test proving untouched internal vocabulary (`FeedSessionRegistry`, `FeedSessionId`, `Nip50SearchSession`, `Nip29Group*Session`, etc.) is never flagged [...] One design call for your eyes: the agent created **`nmp-replies`** as a new concept crate rather than putting the doorway in nmp-nip01/nip22 as #2758's text said. Its reasoning is sound — "replies" as a concept spans NIP-10 kind:1 *and* NIP-22 kind:1111, so a doorway inside nip01 would force a nip01→nip22 dependency — and it did classify both new crates in `release/nmp-release.toml` properly. But it sets the precedent for the other three reads (`nmp-reactions` vs. doorway-in-`nmp-nip25`), so worth a deliberate nod in PR review. [...] Assistant: Filed and cross-linked:

- **[#2797](https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/issues/2797)** — "Concept doorways live in concept crates": relocate `open_search` and the group-feed/group-reaction doorways out of `nmp-native-runtime` into their concept crates via the engine's read-host seam, then un-bundle the runtime's per-NIP dependencies (end state: runtimes implement the seam once, zero per-concept deps, so omitting a concept crate means its symbols don't exist at any layer). Includes the lint ratchet — no `nmp-nip*` deps in runtime crates, no `open_<concept>` defined outside its concept crate — and the "done means" greps. Marked blocked on #2777 steps 1–2, since the spine's host seam defines the shape the relocated doorways consume, with a note to coordinate the search/group-feed relocations with their lane migrations (likely the same PRs).
- **Comment on #2777** registering it as step 7 so the engine issue's sequencing stays the single picture. [...] **#2797** (relocate `open_search`/group doorways out of `nmp-native-runtime`, un-bundle its per-NIP deps) is still OPEN, but a separate agent fleet has been executing it hard while we worked — I can see ~10 merged PRs doing exactly it: `Move native NIP-50 search doorway to nmp-nip50` (#2826), the browser equivalent (#2827), NIP-29 group doorways to concept crates (#2828/#2829), group reactions folded into `nmp-reactions` (#2831), plain reaction doorway removed (#2830), and the dep-gating trio (#2835/#2836/#2837).

Checking it against #2797's own "done means": `nmp-native-runtime`'s Cargo.toml now has almost every concept crate as `optional = true` / feature-gated, and NIP-29/NIP-23 demoted to dev-dependencies. **The tail:** `nmp-nip05` and `nmp-nip18` are still unconditional deps (lines 62–63) — so the "zero per-concept deps" bar isn't fully met yet, which is presumably why #2797 is still open rather than a tracking oversight.
